rules.statement: The value placed in pleadings does not affect recoverable costs in a partition action as no revenue is involved and the documents are exempt from stamp duty.
rules.supporting_quote: As no revenue is involved in a partition action expressly because all pleadings and documents are exempted from stamp duty the value placed in the pleadings has no effect on the recoverable costs. In terms of the provisions of Section 57(1)(a) to (c) costs should be determined in accordance with the rates set out in the Fourth Schedule of the Law and this would be on the appraised value of the lot. 245 The subject matter has been appraised by the Commissioner at the final partition and at that stage there appeared to be no objection regarding the correctness and veracity of the valuation. It is belated to attack the appraisement now and the pro-rata costs have to be borne by the parties in terms of Section 57(2) of the Partition Law

rules.statement: Pro-rata costs should be determined according to the rates set out in the Fourth Schedule of the Law and would be based on the appraised value of the lot as assessed by the Commissioner.
